P&O

Brendan and Caoimhin play this in C minor on their album “A Moment of Madness.” C minor! It never occurred to me to play anything ever in C minor! But I sat down with it and it sits pretty easy on the banjo and C#/D box.

Tweak

The P&O, X:2

This setting comes from Jim Moriarity of Boston and Killarney, who follows it with Top of the Maol and Tom Billy’s (https://thesession.org/tunes/3454 and https://thesession.org/tunes/239). It’s a helluva tune and I understand is named after the shipping company. I heard it, understandably, as the Piano.

The P&O, X:11 (in Dmin)

I’ve always enjoyed playing the P&O in this lower key on the fiddle and it just sounds great in Dminor in general. Of course, this is partly inspired by Breanndán and Caoimhín playing it in a veeery “flat” key but there’s a different logic behind that: Breanndán recorded it on an ancient Hohner box tuned in Bb while actually using the Emin fingering (hence that growly Cmin on their album FYH). However, ever since hearing that recording I couldn’t get over the fact that it sounds too “normal” in E, so I settled for D instead :-D

↳ Posted by Bregolas on April 1st, 2024.
